expected.summary: Seventy nine minutes before the anchor a config change (AUTH-512) raised the session TTL for remember_me logins on every auth pod from 24h to 30d. Remember-me sessions stopped expiring after a day, so the sessions Redis that auth keeps sessions in grew steadily: from sixty nine minutes before the anchor auth-1 logged a WARN every five minutes with used_memory climbing from 2.6 GiB towards maxmemory 4 GiB, under maxmemory-policy noeviction. Nine minutes before the anchor it reached the limit. With noeviction Redis still serves reads but refuses writes, and auth.verify refreshes the session on every call; older keys still expire and free a little room, so about one auth.verify in five fails with ReplyError: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'. Every route verifies the session first, so about a fifth of requests on every route fail, and the failures propagate through web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. auth's redis.get spans stay fast and auth's version did not change. The user-profile rollout from 1.4.2 to 1.5.1, four minutes before the failures, is unrelated: user-profile serves no errors of its own and its requests fail only at auth.
contributingFactors: the AUTH-512 change keeping remember_me sessions for 30 days
the sessions Redis running maxmemory-policy noeviction, so a full instance refuses writes
auth.verify writing to the session on every request

criteria.description: Does the brief place the origin at auth, with the AUTH-512 change to a 30 day remember_me session TTL filling the sessions Redis to maxmemory, and noeviction refusing auth's session writes so a share of auth.verify calls fail on every route? 5 = the TTL change, the full Redis, the refused writes and edge-gateway as the victim. Naming only the OOM error scores at most 3.

Is it grounded in the used_memory warnings climbing for an hour before the failures, the config.change lines on auth an hour and a quarter before, the OOM ReplyError on auth spans and the failures spread across every route? Cap at 3 unless it connects the TTL change to the memory growth.
Does it avoid blaming the user-profile 1.5.1 rollout, a traffic surge, a deploy on auth or edge-gateway?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
